<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is safe to source and fetch sources with `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The only executable code in the global scope or in `pkgver()` is a call to `cd "$_pkgname"` followed by `git describe` and `sed`, or a fallback using `git rev-list` and `git rev-parse`. These commands operate solely on the local git repository that will be cloned from the declared upstream (`https://github.com/skammer/somars.git`), which is consistent with standard AUR packaging practices. There is no command substitution, network request, or file operation outside the package build directory that could lead to data exfiltration or remote code execution during sourcing.

The `source` array uses a `git+https` URL pointing to the project's own upstream, which is expected. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is acceptable for this audit stage, as it does not enable code execution during source fetching or PKGBUILD sourcing. The `pkgver()` function is used to compute a version string from git history and does not invoke any payloads or external scripts. All operations are confined to the build environment and are part of normal VCS package workflows.

No obfuscated code, dangerous command substitutions, or unexpected side effects are present in the top-level or `pkgver()` function. The commands run during this phase are limited to version computation and source fetching, both of which are safe in this context.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious code execution during source fetch or PKGBUILD sourcing</summary>
</security_assessment>

It fetches the source from the declared upstream Git repository (`https://github.com/skammer/somars`), which is appropriate and expected. The use of `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is normal for VCS packages and not inherently unsafe, as checksums cannot be determined in advance for Git sources.

The build process uses Cargo (Rust's package manager) in offline or frozen mode where possible, first attempting `--frozen --release` and falling back to `--offline --release` if needed. This prioritizes reproducible builds using previously fetched dependencies. The `prepare()` function pre-fetches dependencies, which is a common technique to ensure they are available for offline builds. All operations are confined to the build directory and respect standard AUR packaging practices.

No suspicious network activity, obfuscated code, or unauthorized system modifications are present. The package installs only the compiled binary and license file into appropriate system directories. Everything aligns with typical Rust-based AUR packaging workflows.
